about: What each kind of part does in a song, how Semitone writes it, how it should sit in the mix, what the song doctor checks, and which extra parts each style and producer tends to use. Read by Add a part, producer passes, emotion rules, the song doctor, the mix and the lessons. Style and producer notes describe musical habits, based on how they're known to work; they never copy melodies, lyrics or recordings. Agreed with Jamie 6 Nov 2026.

lead.name: Melody
lead.does: Carries the song: the line the singer sings and the hook people remember.
lead.relation: the reference every other part is measured against

mix.eq: presence 2–5 kHz; nothing else may mask this band while the lead sings

counter.name: Counter melody
counter.does: A second melody that answers the lead: it moves when the lead rests or holds, and holds when the lead moves.
counter.relation: complementary rhythm, mostly a 3rd or 6th away, contrary or oblique motion
counter.sections: verse 2 onwards and choruses; rarely verse 1, which should stay bare

mix.pan: opposite side to any panned guitar, 20–40% off centre
mix.eq: dip 2–4 kHz by 2 dB while the lead sings

harmony.name: Harmony / backing vocal
harmony.does: Sings with the lead on the same words, usually a diatonic 3rd above or a 6th below, to make a line feel bigger.
harmony.relation: parallel to the lead, same rhythm and lyrics
harmony.sections: choruses and the last line of a verse; whole song only for stacked styles

mix.eq: high-pass 150 Hz, softer 3 kHz than the lead

double.name: Double / octave
double.does: The same line again, in unison or an octave away, to thicken or brighten it.

mix.pan: unison doubles wide (±60%), octave doubles centre

chords.name: Chords
chords.does: Plays the harmony and sets the colour of each section.
chords.relation: voicings stay below the lead's lowest note in its range

pad.name: Pad / strings bed
pad.does: Long held notes that glue the chords together and fill the space without drawing attention.
pad.relation: holds chord tones, smallest movement between chords (voice leading)
pad.sections: builds: choruses, bridges, last chorus; often out in verse 1

arp.name: Arpeggio
arp.does: Plays the chord one note at a time in a repeating pattern, adding motion and pulse.
arp.relation: chord tones only, pattern locked to the grid (8ths or 16ths)

bass.name: Bass
bass.does: Roots the harmony and locks with the kick.
bass.relation: root or chord tone on beat 1 of each chord

bass2.name: Second bass
bass2.does: A second low part: a sub under the bass, an octave above it, or a synth bass layered with a real one.
bass2.relation: kinds: sub (octave below, sine, follows roots), octave (above, brighter), layer (same notes, other sound)
bass2.sections: usually choruses and drops; out in verses so the low end breathes

mix.eq: sub: only below 80 Hz and high-pass the main bass at ~60 Hz; octave: high-pass 120 Hz

drums.name: Drums
drums.does: The groove and the energy of each section.

mix.eq: kick and bass share the low end: duck one under the other

perc.name: Extra percussion
perc.does: Shaker, tambourine, claps or toms that lift a section without changing the beat.
perc.relation: off-beats and 16ths the kit leaves empty

texture.name: Texture / FX
texture.does: Risers, reverses, field sounds and swells that mark changes between sections.
texture.sections: the last bar before a new section

loop.name: Loop
loop.does: A dropped-in audio loop (e.g. from Splice), fitted to the song's tempo and key.

mix.eq: high-pass 150 Hz unless it is a bass or drum loop

audio.name: Audio part
audio.does: A recorded voice or instrument; its role (lead, harmony, guitar, …) is chosen when recording.

steps: Find the gaps: beats where the lead rests, holds a note longer than a beat, or the phrase ends.
Put the counter's movement in those gaps; while the lead moves, the counter holds or rests.
Choose notes from the current chord first, then the scale; on strong beats use chord tones.
Keep it a 3rd, 6th or 10th from the lead when both sound; never a minor 2nd, major 7th or minor 9th on a strong beat.
Prefer contrary or oblique motion to the lead; avoid parallel 5ths and octaves with it.
Stay in its own register: at least a 4th below or above the lead's tessitura, never crossing it for more than a beat.
Echo one small rhythmic or melodic idea from the hook so it sounds related, not random.
Thin it in verses, fullest in the last chorus.
variants: inner line (between lead and chords, slow)

steps: Copy the lead's rhythm and lyrics.
Move each note to the diatonic 3rd above (or 6th below); if that clashes with the chord, use the nearest chord tone.
Smooth leaps bigger than a 4th that the lead doesn't make.
Only on the lines the style harmonises (see styleParts); default: chorus lines and the last line of a verse.
Sub: one octave under Bass, roots only, sustained, sine or triangle.
Octave: one octave above, same rhythm, brighter sound.
Layer: same notes, a different sound (e.g. synth on real bass).
Default sections: choruses and drops; out in verses.
Take the chord tones in the arp's register.
Pattern by style: up, up-down, broken (1-5-8-10), or pedal (root between each tone).
Rate by tempo: 16ths under 100 BPM, 8ths above 120 BPM.
Re-voice at each chord change with the smallest movement.
Hold the chord's 3rd and 7th (or 5th) for the whole chord.
Move each voice to the nearest tone of the next chord.
Open in the chorus (wider spread), close in the verse.
Fill the 16ths or off-beats the drums leave empty.
Shaker or tambourine in choruses, claps on 2 and 4 in builds.
A linked copy of another part: same notes, its own sound, octave, level, effects and sections.
Unlink to make an independent copy.

doctor.check: A minor 2nd, major 7th or minor 9th between the lead and any melody-family part on a strong beat.
doctor.fix: Move the other part to the nearest chord tone.

doctor.check: A counter or harmony sits within 2 semitones of the lead's register for more than two bars while both sound.
doctor.fix: Move it an octave, or into the lead's gaps.

doctor.check: Lead and counter both move (notes shorter than a beat) at the same time for more than a bar.
doctor.fix: Hold the counter while the lead moves.

doctor.check: Parallel 5ths or octaves between lead and counter (shown as a taste note, not an error).
doctor.fix: Use contrary motion on one of them.

doctor.check: Two low parts (bass, bass2, low pad) both above −18 dB below 150 Hz in the same section.
doctor.fix: High-pass one, or drop Bass 2 in that section.

doctor.check: More than three melody-family parts sound at once.
doctor.fix: Mute one for that section, or make it a layer.

doctor.check: An extra part plays in verse 1 and every later section, so nothing builds.

euphoric.mix: widen extra parts on the chorus downbeat

intimate.keep: lead, one chord part, maybe bass

add: counter answer rising at phrase ends
counter on a vintage keys or strings sound
double an octave up on the hook
double of the lead an octave up, quiet
double of the lead in unison

triumphant.mix: everything wider and brighter in the last chorus

add: counter inner line, slow, late in the song
double of the lead, detuned and quiet
double of the lead in unison
harmony a 4th or 5th on the hook
counter answer, slow, on a breathy sound
counter descant on strings in the chorus

lonely.keep: one sparse part and the lead

partMoves.about: Producer-pass and emotion moves that add, change or remove parts. Grammar: add:<role>[:<variant>]@<where>, layer:<part>:<sound>@<where>, drop:<role>@<where>, thin:<role>@<where>. <where> uses the same section words as other moves (verse1, chorus, last-chorus, all). Each added part is suggested with a reason and its own switch, like any move.

chappell.notes: Big stacked backing vocals and harmonies in choruses; 80s synth arps and bright synth counter lines.

gaga.notes: Stacked vocal harmonies, synth bass doubling the bass in choruses, sequenced synth arps.

gaga-joanne.notes: Acoustic and country-rock: harmony a 3rd above in choruses, guitar fills answering the vocal.

gaga-mayhem.notes: Layered synth and live bass, doubled vocals, guitars as counter riffs.

fleetwood.notes: Three-part vocal harmonies are central; lead guitar lines answer the vocal; melodic bass moves between chord tones.

fleetwood-blues.notes: Blues guitar fills in call and response with the vocal at the end of each line.

rhcp.notes: The bass often acts as a second melody; guitar fills answer the vocal; high falsetto backing harmonies in choruses.

rhcp-funk.notes: Busy slap bass as the counter line; funk guitar stabs in the gaps.

tiersen.notes: Accordion, toy piano or glockenspiel counter melodies over a repeating piano or strings figure.

tiersen-piano.notes: Left hand ostinato with a right-hand counter melody; layers added one at a time each repeat.

tiersen-postrock.notes: Tremolo guitar layers that build and stack towards a climax.

strangerthings.notes: Analogue synth arpeggios, long pads and a pulsing bass ostinato.

jazz.notes: Horn or piano answers between vocal phrases; walking bass; comping fills the gaps.

charli.notes: Distorted sub bass under the bass, pitched vocal doubles, glitchy FX between sections.

charli-pop.notes: Bright synth stabs, pitched vocal layers, heavy sub in drops.

charli-pop2.notes: Hyperpop: detuned synth arps, distorted sub, stacked pitched vocals.

charli-mff.notes: Club-leaning: sub bass layer and FX risers into drops.

lana-btd.notes: Orchestral strings as a bed and as counter lines, stacked backing vocals, hip-hop drums.

lana-uv.notes: Reverb-heavy guitar lines answering the vocal; sparse, few extra parts; room to breathe.

lana-honeymoon.notes: Slow strings and brass swells as a bed, sustained counter lines under the vocal.

lana-nfr.notes: Piano-led with stacked, doubled backing vocals and slide or Mellotron colour lines.

lana-bb.notes: Mostly piano and voice; at most one gentle counter line or soft strings late in the song.

cinematic.notes: String counter lines, ostinato arps, brass and choir swells, risers into big moments.

country.notes: Harmony vocal a 3rd above in choruses; fiddle, pedal steel or dobro fills answering each vocal line.

edm.notes: Sub plus mid bass (two basses), plucky arps, supersaw layers on the hook, risers into drops.

psych.notes: Fuzz or organ counter riffs, swirling pads, reversed FX, close harmonies.

antonoff.notes: Doubled and octave-stacked vocals, one synth family layered across parts, big room drums in choruses.

maxmartin.notes: Every section has a hook: post-chorus vocal hooks, harmonies that lift the pre-chorus, a counter hook in the last chorus.

finneas.notes: Minimal: whispered doubles close to the lead, a deep sub under sparse parts, few extra lines.

mikedean.notes: Lush synth pads and expressive analogue synth lead lines as counter melodies or solos.

redone.notes: Synth stabs and chant-like group vocals on the hook, heavy synth bass layers.

rubin.notes: Strips songs back: removes extra parts so the voice and one instrument carry it.

nigro.notes: Stacked theatrical harmonies and guitar layers that grow through the song.

agcook.notes: Pitched vocal layers, glossy synth arps and distorted sub bass.
